features.notes: Attempt 1 verified all 10 tasks but a parity-run regression (scrape extracted=4/46, 91% fallback) was caught post-verification by the PM via OpenRouter token logs. Root cause: P1 body-cap category error — DEFAULT_MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH (70000, a prompt-truncation cap) was reused as the raw HTTP fetch-body cap, rejecting ~90% of real article pages. Fix: new DEFAULT_MAX_FETCH_BYTES (5MB) for fetch bodies; DEFAULT_MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH retains its prompt role. Re-verified: extracted=56/60 (93%), all gates green (309 tests). Documented in the feature spec's Post-verification correction section.

failure_reasons: Feature verification: live login does not complete. Browser-SDK createEmailPasswordSession sets a cookie on the Appwrite server domain (appwrite.example.com), which localhost:3000 never receives (cookie domain scoping + third-party cookie blocking). After router.push('/'), middleware finds no a_session cookie and redirects back to /login silently. Per-task verification (build/lint/test/typecheck) passed because it did not exercise the live cross-domain cookie path.
escalations.manager_rescue_plan: Replace client-side browser-SDK login/logout with Next.js server actions. Login action: node-appwrite Client with APPWRITE_API_KEY -> Account.createEmailPasswordSession(email,password) -> capture response.secret -> set HttpOnly first-party cookie a_session_<projectId> on the app domain via cookies().set. Logout action: read cookie secret -> deleteSession('current') via session-bearing client -> clear cookie. Middleware and session.ts read path already consume this cookie unchanged. Login page invokes the server action (useActionState or client component calling the action), shows errors from the action result.
